title: The Effect of Division I College Football on Mental Health

mappings.3862549: The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of Division I college football on the mental health of players. Specifically, the study will examine the relationship between playing Division I college football and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance.
mappings.3862550:
The aim of this study is to examine the mental health of Division I college football players. The specific objectives are to:
1. Examine the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance among Division I college football players.
2. Examine the relationship between playing Division I college football and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance.
3. Examine the relationship between sport-related concussion history and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance among Division I college football players.
mappings.3862551: Mental health concerns among college athletes have become an increasingly important topic in recent years. Research has shown that college athletes may be at an increased risk for mental health issues, including depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance (Wolanin et al., 2016). Football players, in particular, may be at an elevated risk due to the physical demands of the sport, including the risk of concussion and other injuries (Kerr et al., 2014). Despite the growing awareness of mental health concerns among college athletes, there is limited research examining the mental health of Division I college football players specifically. This study will address this gap in the literature by examining the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance among Division I college football players and the relationship between playing Division I college football and these mental health outcomes. Additionally, this study will examine the relationship between sport-related concussion history and mental health outcomes among Division I college football players.
mappings.3862553: Participants will be current Division I college football players at Texas Christian University (TCU). Approximately 100 football players will be recruited to participate in this study. Participants must be at least 18 years of age, a current member of the TCU football team, and able to read and understand English. Participants will be recruited through the TCU football program. The research team will work with the football coaching staff and athletic training staff to identify potential participants and distribute recruitment materials.
mappings.3862561: Participants will complete an online survey through Qualtrics. The survey will include demographic questions, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) to assess depression symptoms, the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) to assess anxiety symptoms, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) to assess sleep disturbance, and questions about sport-related concussion history. The survey will take approximately 15-20 minutes to complete. Participants will complete the survey at one time point during the competitive football season.
mappings.3862579: There are no costs to participants for participating in this study. Participants will not be compensated for their participation.
mappings.3862580: All survey responses will be collected through Qualtrics, a secure online survey platform. Data will be stored on a password-protected computer in the PI's locked office. Only the research team will have access to the data. Participant names will not be collected on the survey. Instead, each participant will be assigned a unique identification number. The link between participant names and identification numbers will be stored in a separate, password-protected file. All data will be stored for a minimum of three years after the completion of the study, after which it will be permanently deleted.
mappings.3862581: Descriptive statistics will be used to examine the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance among participants. Pearson correlations will be used to examine the relationship between concussion history and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance. Multiple regression analyses will be used to examine the relationship between playing Division I college football and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance, controlling for relevant covariates.

mappings.3862869:
Participants will complete an online survey through Qualtrics. The survey will include the following measures:

1. Demographic Questionnaire: Participants will provide demographic information including age, race/ethnicity, year in school, position on the football team, and number of years playing football.

2. Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9): The PHQ-9 is a 9-item self-report measure that assesses the severity of depressive symptoms over the past two weeks. Items are rated on a 4-point Likert scale from 0 (not at all) to 3 (nearly every day). Total scores range from 0 to 27, with higher scores indicating more severe depressive symptoms.

3. Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7): The GAD-7 is a 7-item self-report measure that assesses the severity of anxiety symptoms over the past two weeks. Items are rated on a 4-point Likert scale from 0 (not at all) to 3 (nearly every day). Total scores range from 0 to 21, with higher scores indicating more severe anxiety symptoms.

4. Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI): The PSQI is a 19-item self-report measure that assesses sleep quality and disturbance over the past month. The measure yields seven component scores and one global score. Global scores range from 0 to 21, with higher scores indicating poorer sleep quality.

5. Concussion History Questionnaire: Participants will be asked about their history of sport-related concussions, including the number of concussions sustained, the time since their most recent concussion, and any symptoms experienced following their most recent concussion.

The survey will take approximately 15-20 minutes to complete. Participants will complete the survey at one time point during the competitive football season.

mappings.3863068: The risks associated with this study are minimal. There is a potential risk of emotional discomfort when completing the survey items related to depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance. To minimize this risk, participants will be informed that they may skip any questions that make them feel uncomfortable and that they may withdraw from the study at any time without penalty. Additionally, participants will be provided with contact information for the TCU Counseling Center should they experience any distress as a result of participating in the study. There is also a potential risk of loss of confidentiality. To minimize this risk, participant names will not be collected on the survey, and all data will be stored on a password-protected computer in the PI's locked office.
mappings.3863069: There are no direct benefits to participants for participating in this study. However, the results of this study may help inform future interventions and programming aimed at improving the mental health of Division I college football players. Additionally, this study may contribute to the growing body of literature on the mental health of college athletes.
mappings.3863071: All survey responses will be collected through Qualtrics, a secure online survey platform. Participant names will not be collected on the survey. Instead, each participant will be assigned a unique identification number. The link between participant names and identification numbers will be stored in a separate, password-protected file accessible only to the PI. All data will be stored on a password-protected computer in the PI's locked office. Only members of the research team will have access to the data. Data will be reported in aggregate form only, and no individual participant will be identifiable in any publications or presentations resulting from this study. All data will be stored for a minimum of three years after the completion of the study, after which it will be permanently deleted.
mappings.3863075: Descriptive statistics will be used to examine the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance among participants. Means, standard deviations, and frequencies will be calculated for all study variables. Pearson correlations will be used to examine the relationships between concussion history and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance. Multiple regression analyses will be used to examine the relationship between playing Division I college football and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance, controlling for relevant covariates including age, race/ethnicity, year in school, and position on the football team. All analyses will be conducted using SPSS statistical software. The significance level will be set at p < .05.
